simulator.tau_markerlight_all_detach.quoted_text: Each time a T'AU EMPIRE unit from your army (excluding KROOT units) is selected to shoot, ranged weapons equipped by models in your unit have their Ballistic Skill characteristic improved by 1 and have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability while targeting an enemy unit that is visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units that are not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy models.
simulator.tau_markerlight_all_detach.trigger: any T'au Empire (non-KROOT) detachment is shooting in the simulator's batched Shooting window — gated by env var SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_ALL_DETACH=1 (default OFF). The base sim only ran Battle._run_markerlight_phase for detachments carrying the Mont'ka-only `lethal_hits_on_guided` flag (an early-exit at code/simulator.py), so non-Mont'ka T'au (e.g. Kauyon) received ZERO Guided uptime even though the consumer in code/units.py reads `guided_enemy_uids` without checking that flag.
simulator.tau_markerlight_all_detach.effect: GATE 1 (SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_ALL_DETACH, default OFF, byte-identical when unset): when ON, the base Markerlight phase runs for ALL T'au detachments (the `lethal_hits_on_guided` early-exit is bypassed; the phase still returns when there is no resolved detachment). This restores the army-wide base Guided buff (+1 to the Hit roll and [SUSTAINED HITS 1] vs the marked target) for every T'au detachment and every round, as the rule is army-wide. The Mont'ka-specific Lethal-Hits-on-Guided remains gated on the `lethal_hits_on_guided` flag in Unit.attack and is unchanged by this gate. APPROXIMATION: marking still follows the existing per-carrier model (one carrier marks the highest-points enemy in 36" + line of sight per the per-shot emission rule `simulator.markerlight_emission`); this gate only changes WHICH detachments the phase runs for, not how a single carrier marks.

simulator.tau_markerlight_base_los.rule_name: Markerlights / Guided (line-of-sight condition, not a per-attacker hit roll)
simulator.tau_markerlight_base_los.quoted_text: Each time a T'AU EMPIRE unit from your army (excluding KROOT units) is selected to shoot, ranged weapons equipped by models in your unit have their Ballistic Skill characteristic improved by 1 and have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability while targeting an enemy unit that is visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units that are not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy models.
simulator.tau_markerlight_base_los.trigger: a T'au Empire (non-KROOT) unit shoots an enemy unit that is visible (line of sight) to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units — gated by env var SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_BASE_LOS (ADOPTED default-on, wave 254; SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_BASE_LOS=0 is the kill-switch restoring the legacy hit-roll-gated `guided_enemy_uids`). The verbatim rule grants the buff on the line-of-sight / markerlight-token condition ("while targeting an enemy unit that is visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units"), NOT on a per-attacker Ballistic-Skill hit roll. The base sim instead gates the buff on `Army.guided_enemy_uids`, which is populated only when a per-carrier d6 to-hit roll succeeds inside Battle._run_markerlight_phase — firing the base buff only about half the time the real rule should.
simulator.tau_markerlight_base_los.effect: GATE 2 (SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_BASE_LOS, ADOPTED default-on wave 254, byte-identical to the legacy behaviour when =0): at the default (or =1), Battle._run_markerlight_phase builds `Army.guided_los_enemy_uids` — every alive enemy unit within 36" + line of sight + a legal target (Look Out Sir / Lone Operative) of AT LEAST ONE friendly MARKERLIGHT carrier, with NO per-carrier to-hit roll — and the base Guided buff branches in Unit.attack (the +1-to-Hit hit-modifier branch and the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] sustained-hits branch) read this line-of-sight set instead of `guided_enemy_uids`. The Mont'ka [LETHAL HITS] consumer keeps reading the hit-roll-gated `guided_enemy_uids`, so only the BASE buff's gating changes. When =0 (kill-switch), `guided_los_enemy_uids` is never populated or read and the base buff continues to read `guided_enemy_uids` exactly as the legacy sim did. APPROXIMATION: the simulator has no physical Markerlight token object, so visibility-to-a-MARKERLIGHT-unit is modelled as the carrier's own line of sight + 36" range + target eligibility (the same geometry the per-shot emission gate uses), which is the most defensible faithful reading of "visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units".

simulator.tau_mark_per_phase.rule_name: For the Greater Good — marking happens at the start of YOUR Shooting phase
simulator.tau_mark_per_phase.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is T'AU EMPIRE, at the start of your Shooting phase you can select units from your army with this ability to become Observer units.
simulator.tau_mark_per_phase.trigger: gated by env var SWEG_TAU_MARK_PER_PHASE (default OFF, byte-identical when unset). Battle._run_round currently calls _run_markerlight_phase for BOTH armies once at round start, before either has activated. Its comment justifies this by saying the alternating-activation loop materialises no global Shooting-phase barrier — but the evaluation frame is always VANILLA (--sweghammer is never passed to any anchor), and _run_round_vanilla_turns gives each army its own Movement/Shooting/Charge/Fight block, so a per-army Shooting-phase barrier does exist there.
simulator.tau_mark_per_phase.effect: MEASURABLE FIDELITY COST OF THE BATCHING: because both armies mark before the first player moves, the SECOND player's marks are computed against a board state up to a full enemy turn out of date — stale positions, stale line of sight, and candidate units that may already have been destroyed. The verbatim rule marks at the start of the marking player's OWN Shooting phase, against the board as it then stands. Gate ON: the batched round-start call is skipped in vanilla and _run_markerlight_phase(active, other) runs inside each army's own Shooting-phase block instead (at the _phase_seq boundary in _run_round_vanilla_turns). Alternating activations deliberately KEEP the batched behaviour, since that mode genuinely has no per-army barrier to attach it to. Gate OFF restores the round-start batching exactly; verified byte-identical against narrow digest 16fc8f984d0f7e9d70e4216d and wide ca825421c960cc5dd31ba79c, and verified wired by the gate-ON wide digest 09acc969cf25f9f0c2607d9e. NOTE the change moves when the phase's random Ballistic Skill rolls are consumed, so gate-ON necessarily re-bases the whole random stream — the delta is not attributable to marking quality alone and must be read as a frame comparison.

simulator.tau_markerlight_carriers.rule_name: Pathfinder Team — MARKERLIGHT unit keyword (10e datasheet keyword line)
simulator.tau_markerlight_carriers.quoted_text: KEYWORDS: INFANTRY, GRENADES, MARKERLIGHT, PATHFINDER TEAM
simulator.tau_markerlight_carriers.trigger: Battle._run_markerlight_phase selects the army's Markerlight carriers by the MARKERLIGHT unit keyword. Three datasheets carry MARKERLIGHT on their real 10e keyword line but lacked it in the catalogue, so they never marked: Pathfinder Team, Darkstrider and Firesight Team. Verified 2026-07-29 by reading every keyword line on the T'au Empire datasheets index: exactly eight datasheets carry MARKERLIGHT — Darkstrider, Firesight Team, Breacher Team, Strike Team, Pathfinder Team, Sky Ray Gunship, Stealth Battlesuits and Manta. Manta is a Titanic flyer no archetype fields and is deliberately excluded. iter16 added the keyword to Strike Team, Breacher Team and Sky Ray Gunship from these same keyword lines and omitted the Pathfinder Team, which is the faction's dedicated marking unit and the reason the Guided rule exists — while the Mont'ka archetype seeds it at count=2 EXPLICITLY to guarantee markerlight carriers.
simulator.tau_markerlight_carriers.effect: ADOPTED 2026-07-29. The keyword is hand-entered in data/overrides.json for all three units per CLAUDE.md rule 7 (BSData carries no Markerlight data at all — the string does not appear once in data/bsdata/parsed.json — so every MARKERLIGHT keyword in the catalogue is hand-entered there, exactly as iter16 did for the other three). Darkstrider and Firesight Team keep their CHARACTER / EPIC HERO keywords, since an overrides unit_keywords entry REPLACES the list rather than extending it. No simulator logic changed: the marking geometry, squad deduplication, to-hit roll and both consumer branches in Unit.attack are untouched. MEASURED: Guided uptime over 120 T'au shooting phases went from 0.42 to 0.78 enemy squads marked per phase, zero-mark phases from 68 to 46 percent, share of live enemy squads from 3.5 to 6.5 percent. T'au-scoped paired N=80 screen versus anchor sc69a (36,960 matched games, 439 flips): T'au Empire 48.2 to 51.7, paired +3.50 +-3.37 DECISIVE, moving toward the real 54.3 and taking its gated error from 1.88 to 0.00 (inside the noise band). Gated mean absolute error 2.85 to 2.82. Closed-matrix drift on opponents: four of five decisive movers go toward real (Chaos Space Marines -1.35 off a 61.5-vs-55.6 over-pole, Adeptus Mechanicus -0.94 off 49.2-vs-44.4, Adeptus Custodes +0.71 toward 49.5), one away (Necrons -0.91 from an already-under 49.3 vs 53.5).

simulator.tau_crisis_fireknife_missile_p.rule_name: Crisis Fireknife Battlesuits — wargear (plasma rifle + missile pod equipped simultaneously)
simulator.tau_crisis_fireknife_missile_p.quoted_text: Every model is equipped with: plasma rifle; missile pod; battlesuit fists. [Missile pod: Range 30", A 2, BS 4+, S 7, AP -1, D 2] [Plasma rifle: Range 18", A 1, BS 4+, S 8, AP -3, D 3]
simulator.tau_crisis_fireknife_missile_p.trigger: a Crisis Fireknife Battlesuits unit shoots — every model carries BOTH the plasma rifle and the missile pod as standard wargear and fires both each Shooting phase; gated by env var SWEG_TAU_BATTLESUIT_WEAPONS (adopted default-on, wave 256; set to 0 to disable). BSData v10.6.0 maps only the plasma rifle (parsed.json extra_ranged_profiles is empty), dropping the missile pod — a mapper gap.
simulator.tau_crisis_fireknife_missile_p.effect: By default (or when SWEG_TAU_BATTLESUIT_WEAPONS=1), _build_catalog appends a 'missile pod' profile (Attacks 2, S7, AP-1, Damage 2 mean, Range 30", Ballistic Skill 4+/hit_probability 0.5) to t_au_empire_crisis_fireknife_battlesuits.extra_ranged_profiles. 'missile pod' strips to a distinct weapon root from 'plasma rifle' under _strip_mode_suffix, so the multi-root firing loop in Unit.attack fires both additively (no per-attack code change; mirrors the Hammerhead multi-weapon override). Setting SWEG_TAU_BATTLESUIT_WEAPONS=0 is byte-identical to the legacy behaviour (extra_ranged_profiles stays empty, only the plasma rifle fires).

simulator.tau_crisis_sunforge_second_fus.rule_name: Crisis Sunforge Battlesuits — wargear (2 fusion blasters equipped simultaneously)
simulator.tau_crisis_sunforge_second_fus.quoted_text: Every model is equipped with: 2 fusion blasters; battlesuit fists. [Fusion blaster: Range 12", A 1, BS 4+, S 9, AP -4, D D6]
simulator.tau_crisis_sunforge_second_fus.trigger: a Crisis Sunforge Battlesuits unit shoots — every model carries TWO fusion blasters as standard wargear; gated by env var SWEG_TAU_BATTLESUIT_WEAPONS (adopted default-on, wave 256; set to 0 to disable). BSData v10.6.0 maps only one fusion blaster with attacks=1, dropping the second — a mapper gap. A duplicate 'fusion blaster' extra_ranged_profile would collapse into one mutex group under _strip_mode_suffix, so the second blaster is modelled as attacks=2 on the primary profile.
simulator.tau_crisis_sunforge_second_fus.effect: By default (or when SWEG_TAU_BATTLESUIT_WEAPONS=1), _build_catalog sets attacks=2 on t_au_empire_crisis_sunforge_battlesuits via dataclasses.replace (doubling the attack count of the single mapped fusion-blaster profile). All other fusion-blaster characteristics (S9, AP-4, Damage D6) are unchanged. Setting SWEG_TAU_BATTLESUIT_WEAPONS=0 is byte-identical to the legacy behaviour (attacks stays at the BSData-mapped value of 1).

simulator.tau_sunforge.quoted_text: Each time a model in this unit makes a ranged attack that targets a MONSTER or VEHICLE unit, you can re-roll the Wound roll and you can re-roll the Damage roll.
simulator.tau_sunforge.trigger: a Crisis Sunforge Battlesuits model makes a ranged attack that targets a unit with the MONSTER or VEHICLE keyword; gated by env var SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES (adopted default-on, wave 256; set to 0 to disable) AND tau_sunforge=true on the bearer's UnitProfile (set via overrides.json).
simulator.tau_sunforge.effect: By default (or when SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES=1) and the target carries MONSTER or VEHICLE: att_reroll_all_wounds is set True (re-roll all failed Wound rolls, reusing the existing plumbing); a _sunforge_vs_armour flag is set True which drives a per-shot Damage-dice re-roll in the ranged damage loop (re-roll once if the first dice roll is below the dice mean, the optimal exercise of 'you can re-roll'). Melee attacks are unaffected (ranged-only per the rule). Setting SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES=0 is byte-identical to the legacy behaviour (_sunforge_vs_armour stays False, zero extra random draws).

simulator.tau_armour_hunter.quoted_text: Each time this model makes an attack that targets a MONSTER or VEHICLE, add 1 to the Hit roll.
simulator.tau_armour_hunter.trigger: a Hammerhead Gunship model makes any attack (ranged or melee) that targets a unit with the MONSTER or VEHICLE keyword; gated by env var SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES (adopted default-on, wave 256; set to 0 to disable) AND tau_armour_hunter=true on the bearer's UnitProfile (set via overrides.json).
simulator.tau_armour_hunter.effect: By default (or when SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES=1) and the target carries MONSTER or VEHICLE: hit_mod_delta is incremented by 1 (same mechanism as Righteous Paragons' hit-half, but with no wound bonus). Applies to both ranged and melee attacks per the rule. Setting SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES=0 is byte-identical to the legacy behaviour (hit_mod_delta is unaffected).

simulator.tau_targeting_array.quoted_text: Each time this model is selected to shoot, you can re-roll one Hit roll or you can re-roll one Wound roll when resolving those attacks.
simulator.tau_targeting_array.trigger: a Hammerhead Gunship model is selected to shoot (ranged attacks only); gated by env var SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES (adopted default-on, wave 256; set to 0 to disable) AND tau_targeting_array=true on the bearer's UnitProfile (set via overrides.json).
simulator.tau_targeting_array.effect: By default (or when SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES=1): _chiv_wound_reroll is set True once per shooting activation, granting one per-activation Wound-die re-roll via the existing single-slot Code-Chivalric Wound re-roll machinery. APPROXIMATION: the rule allows re-rolling EITHER one Hit OR one Wound die; we always spend it on a Wound die (the higher-value choice for an anti-armour Railgun where the wound roll is the bottleneck). Setting SWEG_TAU_SUNFORGE_HAMMERHEAD_ABILITIES=0 is byte-identical to the legacy behaviour (_chiv_wound_reroll is unaffected by this gate).

simulator.tau_markerlight_ignores_cover.rule_name: For the Greater Good — MARKERLIGHT [IGNORES COVER] (T'au Empire army rule, 10e)
simulator.tau_markerlight_ignores_cover.quoted_text: Until the end of the phase, each time a model from your army in a Guided unit makes an attack that targets a Spotted unit, improve the Ballistic Skill characteristic of that attack by 1 and, if the Spotted unit was marked by an Observer unit that has the Markerlight keyword, that attack has the [IGNORES COVER] ability.
simulator.tau_markerlight_ignores_cover.trigger: SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_IGNORES_COVER default-on (ADOPTED 2026-07-01; '0' is the byte-identical kill-switch); a T'au Empire Guided unit fires a ranged attack at a Spotted enemy marked by a MARKERLIGHT-keyword Observer unit, modelled as target.uid in Army.guided_los_enemy_uids (the set is built exclusively from MARKERLIGHT-keyword carriers in Battle._run_markerlight_phase, so every uid in it satisfies the Markerlight-Observer condition). BSData source rule id eeb6-c42-48f7-cc21 (T'au Empire.cat.gz).
simulator.tau_markerlight_ignores_cover.effect: That ranged attack gains the [IGNORES COVER] ability — the target's Benefit of Cover save bonus is not applied. Implemented as a third OR-arm in the ignore_cover boolean in Unit.attack (code/units.py ~2147), gated on SWEG_TAU_MARKERLIGHT_IGNORES_COVER=1 and the T'au faction + guided_los_enemy_uids membership; off-path byte-identical (the kill-switch '0' short-circuits the arm). A companion AI target-bias (_tau_guided_target_bonus, a 2x score multiplier toward guided_los_enemy_uids members) was built and screened but REJECTED and removed — it over-concentrated fire and dragged the metric (T'au-scoped N=80 vs sc24a: rule-only gated 2.50 -> 2.49, rule+bias 2.50 -> 2.51, with decisive collateral on Adeptus Mechanicus / Drukhari); only the [IGNORES COVER] rule is adopted. No KROOT exclusion — KROOT units that carry the For the Greater Good ability are legitimately Guided (the earlier investigation's 'excluding KROOT' was a misread of the separate Markerlight Precision boarding-patrol rule).

simulator.tau_nova_charge.quoted_text: Once per battle, when this unit is selected to shoot in your Shooting phase, select one ranged weapon equipped by this model. Until the end of the phase, that weapon has the [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] ability.
simulator.tau_nova_charge.trigger: SWEG_TAU_NOVA_CHARGE default-on (ADOPTED 2026-07-01; '0' is the byte-identical kill-switch); a T'au Riptide Battlesuit (tau_nova_charge=True, set via data/overrides.json) is selected to shoot and has not yet used Nova Charge this battle (tracked in Battle._tau_nova_charge_used)
simulator.tau_nova_charge.effect: The unit's ranged weapons gain [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] for the phase (Battle._apply_nova_charge sets transient_devastating_wounds via _set_transient_squad, once per Riptide per battle). BSData source: T'au Empire.cat.gz Riptide Abilities profile id 8fb6-aff7-75ac-f206 (verified verbatim). APPROXIMATION: the codex grants [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] to ONE chosen ranged weapon; the sim grants the transient to the whole unit for the phase — the same whole-unit approximation as Unholy Bloodshed (simulator.csm_unholy_bloodshed) and Daemonic Ordnance. T'au-scoped paired N=80 vs sc29a: T'au +1.74 (51.2 -> 52.9, toward its real 54.3), gated 2.37 -> 2.35 (collateral Imperial Knights -0.70 toward-real, Adeptus Custodes -0.62). Off path (SWEG_TAU_NOVA_CHARGE=0) the flag is never read — byte-identical.
